text:
anya: FYI bringing up prismatic13b conversion; float16 baseline looks good but int4 quant gives weird headwise rotary artifacts on long summaries. reproducing on our longctx suite now. :thinking:

mike: can you share the exact convert + quant args you used? and a minimal prompt that shows it?

anya: convert command:
```
./convert_model --from hf --to redwood --model prismatic13b --rotary-mode headwise --rotary-scale default
./quantize --mode int4 --calibrate --perchannel --group-size 128
```
Minimal repro prompt: `Summarize the following conversation in three bullets:` + big 3k token thread.

anya: quick eval numbers (longctx-3k bench):
- float16: ROUGE-L 46.2, avg latency 220ms
- int4:   ROUGE-L 40.8, avg latency 86ms
- embed cosine (f16 vs int4): mean 0.958 -> 0.927 (delta -0.031)

ram: that ROUGE drop screams rotary head misalignment or head-permute when folding into int4 kernels. prismatic uses head-interleave layout (headstride != 1) right?

anya: yep head_dim order is interleaved (H, groups, head_stride) — conversion code tried to canonicalize but we may have left a stride mismatch in rotary index map.

mike: can you dump a tiny head map and rotary phase for head 0..7? command: `python -m redwood.tools.dump_headmap --model prismatic13b --heads 0-7`

anya: pasted output (trimmed):
```
head 0: proj shape (64, 4096), rotary_scale=1.0, phase_idx base=0
head 1: proj shape (64, 4096), rotary_scale=1.0, phase_idx base=64
head 2: proj shape (64, 4096), rotary_scale=0.98, phase_idx base=128
head 3: proj shape (64, 4096), rotary_scale=0.98, phase_idx base=192
```
Weird: two heads have 0.98 scale baked in from the checkpoint, others 1.0.

ram: oh that explains asymmetric behavior when quantized — our int4 kernel folds rotary_scale into the quant table and expects uniform scale per head-block. non-uniform scales cause aliasing.

anya: quick experiment: patched loader to normalize rotary_scale per-head to 1.0 (divide out stored scale and put it as a per-head multiplier applied in float before quant). Re-ran int4 bench: ROUGE-L 44.9 (delta vs f16 -1.3), embed cosine 0.946. Huge improvement.

mike: nice find. does that change inference latency or memory?

anya: negligible latency change (88ms), added a tiny pre-multiply on dequant path. memory same.

julie: suggest we add a unit test in convert pipeline to detect per-head rotary_scale variance and either warn or canonicalize. open a PR so infra/ops can review quant implications. :+1:

anya: opened PR <https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4278|#4278> with the normalization patch and a regression test using the longctx suite. CI ran and caught a failing int4 kernel unit in one runner.

ci-bot: build 2981-int4-smoke failed on ubuntu-arm-latest: `test_quant_kernels::headwise_scale_test` — segfault in dequant path.

mike: hmm the arm kernel path has a different codegen for fused multiply; ram can you take a look?

ram: on it — will repro locally and push a small fix to branch. once fixed, we should re-run the longctx regression job and then promote the patch to dedicated-conversions.

anya: thanks — happy to help validate. adding the failing sample to the repro set so it won't regress again. :eyes:
